toolu_01Y2HqeBFC44hkVAffaMD3Bo.command:
cat > /tmp/marlow_vault_task.txt <<'EOF'
WRITE A SPEC: how Clayrune's secrets vault protects keys from agents and survives unattended restarts. Output: docs/VAULT_KEY_PROTECTION_SPEC.md (commit it on your own branch; Dave merges). Decision-ready, not an essay.

CONTEXT (verify against code and the gitignored journal docs/_journal/vault-keyring-remint-2026-09-15.md; don't read any secret values):
- The vault (mc/secrets_store.py, docs/SECRETS.md) holds website logins + TOTP typed into the built-in browser pane via {{user:}}/{{secret:}}/{{totp:}} placeholders, tokens injected into CLI child processes by tools/with-secret.py (args/env), and API keys.
- The master key lived in Windows Credential Manager + a DPAPI mirror. It was lost twice (Sep 8 and Sep 14 Windows Update auto-restarts with no interactive logon; Clayrune's autostart runs pre-login as an S4U task whose credentials die at reboot and which can't use DPAPI). 8 of 10 secrets were lost for good.
- In-flight fix (branch clayrune/agent/daf9c16c955f-vault-review + builder 37aaa8c923bb): a file-backed key in ~/.clayrune/secrets.key with an owner-only ACL, fingerprint, recovery key, pane/serve-file/fence hardening. Ron's objection, 2026-09-15: "not so safe design, anyone who reads the key file and secrets.json can decrypt every saved login."
- Wren's security review of the file-key branch: agents run as the same OS user with full tool access (--dangerously-skip-permissions), so any same-user process can read a file the server reads unattended; header checks cannot tell an agent from a human; the browser pane can reach Clayrune's own origin.
- Ron's constraints: autostart must keep running BEFORE login (unattended restarts); secrets must NOT depend on Windows quirks; cross-platform (Windows, macOS, Linux); installers currently run WITHOUT admin (installer/install.ps1 per-user; install.sh).
- Ron proposed a design to evaluate: a Windows service 'ClayruneKeyBroker' under a dedicated virtual service account; the vault in C:\ProgramData\Clayrune\Vault with ACL SYSTEM + NT SERVICE\ClayruneKeyBroker only; keys encrypted with CNG/DPAPI, preferably TPM-backed; Clayrune talks to it over a secured named pipe; the broker authenticates the requesting user/session, allows only predefined operations, and makes the external API request itself so raw keys never return to Clayrune, extensions, agents, terminals, logs or plugins.
- Dave's evaluation of that proposal: (1) the separate account is the only real boundary against same-user agents, and service-account DPAPI survives unattended restarts; (2) most of our secrets are NOT proxiable API calls (browser logins, TOTP, CLI tokens get released to a process that then sees them); (3) the broker can't tell Clayrune from an agent running as the same user, which is fine for use-without-seeing; (4) it needs admin install, per-OS implementations, and a recovery path because TPM keys die with the hardware.

THE SPEC MUST:
1. Threat model table: who can read what today, with the file key, with a passphrase unlock, with the broker, with a TPM-bound key. Actors: same-user agent, other local user, malware as the user, disk thief/backup leak, remote attacker via tunnel.
2. Options compared on: protection vs same-user agents, unattended restart, cross-platform effort, install elevation, recovery story, UX cost, build size. Include passphrase-derived key (mc/secrets_store.py already has _scrypt_key), file key, broker service, a TPM/Secure Enclave key, and a HYBRID (e.g. broker or passphrase for high-value secrets, a file key for low-value unattended ones).
3. A secret-use taxonomy: which consumption paths can be proxied (never released) vs must release a value, and how each option handles release (per-use approval, audit, scoping, time-boxed).
4. One recommendation with a phased build plan (what ships first and fixes the incident class, what comes later), plus the macOS/Linux equivalents of the broker (launchd daemon / systemd user and Keychain / Secure Enclave / kernel keyring).
5. Name the decisions Ron must make, as a short list with the recommended answer marked.
Keep it under ~1,200 words plus tables. No code changes. Dispatched, so no email, no server restart. Final message: the spec path + commit sha, the recommendation in 3 lines, and the decisions list.
EOF
python -c "
import json,sys
t=open(sys.argv[1],encoding='utf-8').read()
open(sys.argv[2],'w',encoding='utf-8').write(json.dumps({'character':'global:prd-writer','notify_session':'953fd4139ed6','task':t}))
" /tmp/marlow_vault_task.txt /tmp/marlow_vault_body.json && curl -s -X POST http://localhost:5199/api/project/mission_control/agent/dispatch -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @/tmp/marlow_vault_body.json
